chapters.title: Chapter 501: The Mystery Of Blackridge
paragraphs: As Stan explained everything he knew about the situation, the commissioner’s tone gradually became more serious. What had initially sounded like a routine conversation about the prison break had clearly taken on a different level of importance once the details surrounding Blackridge Correctional Facility became clear.
“That’s... extremely troublesome.”
Stan’s eyebrows furrowed slightly at the commissioner’s choice of words. “Why?”
“Because Blackridge isn’t an ordinary facility.”

The moment he heard that, Stan’s expression sharpened. He already knew Blackridge was supposed to be a high-security prison, but the commissioner’s tone suggested there was more to the facility than its reputation alone.
The commissioner continued after a brief pause. “Some of the Red Serpent’s core members are being held there.”
Stan’s eyes widened slightly. “Seriously?”
“Yes.”
“Even their leader?”
“Especially their leader.”

Stan leaned back against the sofa, his expression becoming thoughtful as he processed the information. He had known that several major members of the Red Serpent had been arrested following the authorities’ efforts to dismantle the organization, but he hadn’t realized that so many of them had been concentrated in the same facility.
The fact that the organization’s leader was also being held there made the situation considerably more concerning.
“Damn.”

The word escaped Stan quietly as his mind began connecting the pieces. If the prison really housed that many important members of the Red Serpent, then the consequences of a large-scale escape could be far more serious than the authorities were currently willing to admit.
His gaze instinctively shifted toward Camilla.

She had only been listening to his side of the conversation, so she couldn’t hear the commissioner’s responses, but she had been around Stan long enough to read his expressions. The relaxed demeanor she had displayed while playing chess with him had disappeared completely. Her attention was now fixed on him, and the slight narrowing of her eyes made it obvious that she had realized something serious had happened.
Stan returned his attention to the phone.
“How could prisoners break out of a place like that so easily?”
“They shouldn’t be able to.”
The commissioner’s response came immediately, without hesitation.
“That’s exactly the problem.”
Stan frowned. The certainty in the man’s voice made the situation even more suspicious.
“Meaning?”
“Blackridge is heavily secured. It has multiple layers of security, armed guards, reinforced cells, surveillance systems, and strict restrictions on prisoner movement.”
The commissioner paused briefly before continuing, and when he spoke again, the tension in his voice was even more noticeable.
“For a large number of prisoners to escape at once, something significant must have happened.”
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
“So you don’t know what caused it?”
“Not yet.”
The commissioner’s answer was straightforward, but Stan could tell from his tone that the investigation was already underway.
“I’m going to find out.”
Stan remained silent for a moment before asking the question that had been occupying his mind ever since he heard about the prison break.
“Can you check whether Damien Bale was recaptured?”
“I’ll need some time.”
“Of course.”
Another brief silence settled between them. Stan could almost imagine the commissioner weighing his next words before finally speaking again.
“And Stan?”
“Yeah?”
“If you’re asking about Damien specifically...” The commissioner paused, his voice becoming more cautious as he chose his words. “Is there something I should know?”
Stan’s gaze hardened slightly.
“Not yet.”
He deliberately kept his answer vague. There were certain things he wasn’t prepared to explain, especially when he didn’t yet have enough information himself to determine exactly what had happened.

The commissioner remained silent for a moment. He seemed to understand that Stan was deliberately withholding something, but rather than pressing him for an explanation, he simply accepted the answer.
“Understood.”
“I just want to know whether he’s among the prisoners who escaped.”
“I’ll check.”
“Thanks.”
“Don’t mention it.”
The call ended shortly afterward.

Stan lowered the phone slowly and placed it on the table beside him. His movements were calm, but his expression remained serious as he stared at the device for several seconds, his mind still occupied by everything the commissioner had told him.
The room itself remained quiet.

The chessboard was still positioned between Stan and Camilla, and the pieces remained exactly where they had been before the call. The soft lighting cast a warm glow across the table, creating an atmosphere that should have felt peaceful.
Only a short while ago, Stan had been enjoying the quiet evening with Camilla, completely focused on the game and considering his next move.
Now, the chessboard might as well have not existed.
Camilla studied him from across the table before finally breaking the silence.
“You think this Damien escaped?”
“I don’t know.”
And he genuinely didn’t.

Stan lowered his gaze toward the chessboard and studied the pieces for a moment. The black and white figures stood beneath the room’s soft lighting, frozen in the positions they had occupied before the phone rang. There was something almost ironic about seeing the game sitting there untouched when his mind had suddenly become occupied by an entirely different kind of conflict.
His thoughts returned to Blackridge.
It wasn’t some ordinary prison.
Stan already knew that much.

Blackridge Correctional Facility had been specifically designed to house dangerous criminals who posed a serious threat to society. Its security measures were considerably more advanced than those of ordinary correctional facilities, with multiple layers of protection intended to prevent prisoners from escaping or moving through the facility without authorization.

Every important aspect of the prison’s operation was supposed to be tightly controlled. Prisoner movement was restricted, guards were stationed throughout the facility, surveillance systems monitored the premises, and the cells themselves were reinforced against forced escapes.
A facility like that wasn’t supposed to experience a prison break involving a large number of inmates.
More importantly, some of the Red Serpent’s highest-ranking members were being held there.

The authorities had gone to considerable lengths to capture those criminals. Many were considered extremely dangerous, and some had managed to evade law enforcement for years before finally being brought into custody.
It made little sense for so many of them to end up in the same facility if that facility could apparently be breached so easily.
For that many prisoners to escape simultaneously, something had gone seriously wrong.
Stan’s expression gradually became more serious as he considered the possibilities.
It could have been an internal security failure. Perhaps someone inside the facility had deliberately disabled part of the security system or assisted the prisoners in escaping.
It could have been an attack from outside, with someone powerful enough to breach Blackridge and create an opportunity for the inmates to flee.

There was also the possibility of deliberate assistance from someone working within the facility. If an individual with sufficient authority had betrayed the prison from the inside, they could potentially have created an opening that ordinary prisoners would never have been able to exploit.
And there were other possibilities as well.
Without more information, there was simply no way to determine what had actually happened.
That uncertainty bothered Stan more than anything else.
None of the possibilities were reassuring.
Then there was Damien Bale.
Stan still didn’t know whether Damien had escaped.
He didn’t know whether the man had already been recaptured, whether he had remained inside the facility, or whether he had somehow disappeared during the chaos.
There were simply too many unanswered questions.

chapters.title: Chapter 502: New Variable
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Stan slowly leaned back against the sofa, his fingers resting against the armrest as he considered what Damien might do if he had actually managed to escape.
Damien wasn’t someone Stan could afford to ignore.

The man had already caused enough trouble in the past, and allowing him to disappear completely would create an unpredictable variable that Stan couldn’t account for. As long as Damien remained imprisoned, the situation was relatively straightforward. The authorities could deal with him, and Stan wouldn’t have to concern himself with the matter.
But if Damien was free...
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
Then everything could change.
"I hope I’m wrong," he said quietly.
Camilla’s eyes remained fixed on him.
"About what?"
Stan reached toward the chessboard and picked up one of the pieces, slowly turning it between his fingers as he considered the possibilities.
"About Damien being one of the ones who got out."
His voice remained calm, but the relaxed atmosphere that had existed earlier was gone.
Camilla didn’t respond immediately. She simply watched him, seemingly understanding that Stan’s concern wasn’t based on certainty. It was the potential consequences that bothered him.
Stan eventually lowered his hand and carefully returned the chess piece to the board.
For a moment, neither of them spoke.

Outside, the city continued moving as it always did. Cars traveled along the streets, their headlights occasionally sweeping across the windows. People went home from work, met with friends, ate dinner, or simply enjoyed another ordinary evening without knowing that anything significant had happened.
To anyone looking from the outside, nothing had changed.
But Stan knew better.

Major changes rarely announced themselves immediately. Sometimes they began with something seemingly insignificant, something that could easily be dismissed as an isolated incident until its consequences gradually spread.

The world had already been moving quietly toward something much larger for some time. Events that initially appeared unrelated were beginning to intersect, and this prison break had introduced yet another unknown variable into an already complicated situation.
Stan looked at the chessboard again, his fingers resting lightly against the edge of the table.
The game had been interrupted by a single phone call, but somehow the chessboard now felt strangely appropriate.
One piece had moved.
Then another.
And now a piece had disappeared entirely from the board.
Stan didn’t know who had moved it, where it had gone, or what its next move would be.
He simply knew that the game was no longer as simple as it had been before.
And somewhere out there, Damien Bale might have just become another piece on the board.
The only question was where that piece would appear next.
Across from him, Camilla remained seated in her chair.
"Whoever this Damien is, the strength of the new-age humans can’t compare to yours."
"No. That’s not what concerns me." Stan’s eyes narrowed as he finally looked toward her. "I’ve got people to protect. And something about this doesn’t add up."
Camilla studied him for a moment.

Stan wasn’t the kind of person who became unsettled simply because something unexpected happened. He had encountered situations far stranger than a prison break and dealt with dangerous enemies before.
If he was concerned now, there was clearly something about the incident that didn’t sit right with him.
Before Camilla could respond, Stan’s phone suddenly vibrated against the table.
The unexpected sound immediately drew his attention.
He glanced down.
The commissioner’s name was displayed across the screen.
Stan’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The timing was almost suspiciously convenient.
He had just asked the commissioner to find out whether Damien was among the escaped prisoners or had already been recaptured. If the commissioner was calling now, he had probably found something.
Without hesitation, Stan picked up the phone.
"Commissioner?"
"Stan."

The commissioner’s voice sounded different from before. The casual tone he had used during their earlier conversation was gone, replaced by something considerably more serious. There was a noticeable tension in his voice, as though whatever information he had uncovered wasn’t something he was comfortable discussing casually over the phone.
Stan immediately straightened.
"I’ve got the information you asked for."
Stan’s expression hardened.
He already had a feeling he wasn’t going to like what came next.
"You found out about Damien?
"You found out about Damien?"
"Yes."

There was a brief silence on the other end of the call. Stan’s expression remained calm, but his attention sharpened immediately. The moment the commissioner had mentioned the prison escape, he had already suspected that Damien Bale might be among those who had disappeared. Hearing confirmation only made the situation more troublesome.
"He’s one of the escapees," the commissioner finally said.

Stan’s expression hardened slightly as he leaned back against the sofa. Damien wasn’t someone he could afford to ignore. The man had already caused enough trouble in the past, and allowing him to disappear completely would create an unpredictable variable that Stan couldn’t account for. If Damien had remained imprisoned, then the situation would have been relatively straightforward. The authorities could deal with him, and Stan wouldn’t have needed to concern himself with the matter.
But now Damien was free.
"I see," Stan replied calmly.
"I figured you’d want to know as soon as possible."
"Tell me what happened."

The commissioner’s voice became more serious as he began explaining what he had learned. "I spoke with the prison administration and the officers who were on duty during the breach. At first, their reports were difficult to believe."
Stan’s brows furrowed slightly. "What did they tell you?"
"They told me that one prisoner essentially tore his way out of his cell."
Stan’s eyebrows rose.
"By himself?"
"That’s what they said."

For a moment, Stan said nothing. The statement sounded absurd on its face. Blackridge Correctional Facility wasn’t an ordinary prison, and its cells weren’t designed to be escaped from through brute strength. Even a physically powerful prisoner shouldn’t have been capable of simply forcing his way through the reinforced security measures.
’Did he awaken?’ Stan sighed, he already had plenty on his hands
The commissioner seemed to take his silence for skepticism.
"While they said that, I didn’t take their word for it," he continued. "I asked the prison heads to send me the surveillance footage covering the incident."
"And?"
"I watched it myself."
The commissioner’s voice lowered slightly.
"That’s when I realized their reports weren’t exaggerated."
Stan’s gaze sharpened. "What did you see?"
The commissioner took a slow breath before answering.
"Damien Bale appears to have awakened some sort of... ability."

’he comprehended dao?!’ Stan, however, remained silent. His expression showed little emotion, although his eyes had become noticeably more focused.
The commissioner continued.
"I know how strange that sounds."
"Go on."
"According to the prison records, Damien was attacked by several inmates shortly after being placed in the general population."
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
"Attacked?"
"Yes. Apparently, some of the inmates recognized him from the news and knew about his background. From what we can tell, they wanted to establish dominance over him. They beat him badly."

There was clear disgust in the commissioner’s voice as he recalled what he had seen in the footage. Prison violence wasn’t exactly unheard of, but the circumstances surrounding Damien’s case had made the incident particularly significant.
Stan remained silent for a moment before asking, "How badly?"
"Badly enough that the officers initially thought he might require medical attention."
"And then?"
"This is where things become strange."
The commissioner paused, as though he was still trying to make sense of what he had witnessed himself.
"Some time later, the surveillance footage shows Damien getting back on his feet."
Stan’s expression changed slightly.
"His injuries had healed?"
"That’s what it looks like."
"Completely?"
"Almost."
The commissioner hesitated before continuing.

"There were no obvious signs of the injuries that should have been visible from the earlier beating. He had been badly injured, but when he stood up again, most of those injuries appeared to have disappeared."
Stan’s fingers began tapping lightly against the armrest of the sofa as he processed the information. His mind immediately began considering the possibilities.
It’s normal for cultivators like him, His sis and Camilla to have enhanced regeneration, but Damien’s own seemed to be on another level...
Though whatever healing Damien is capable of can’t compare with Camillas but it can compete with Stan’s natural healing...
Anyways the commissioner continued speaking before Stan could ask another question.
"Then Damien confronted the same prisoners who attacked him."
"What happened?"
"He beat them."
Stan’s expression remained calm. "That’s not exactly surprising if he was angry."
"Stan..."
The commissioner’s tone became noticeably more serious.
"He didn’t simply overpower them.
"He overwhelmed them."
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
"How?"
"The footage shows him throwing one of the inmates several feet."
The commissioner paused briefly before continuing.
"Another inmate tried to restrain him from behind. Damien grabbed him and threw him into the wall with enough force to knock him down."
"And the third?"
"He was apparently beaten unconscious."
Stan remained silent. He could already tell that the commissioner wasn’t calling merely to tell him that Damien had won a prison fight. There was something more significant about what had happened.
The commissioner confirmed that suspicion a moment later.
"After that, Damien walked over to the cell door."
"And?"
"He bent the bars."
Stan’s expression became even more focused.
"The metal bars?"
"Yes."
"With his hands?"
"Yes."
Silence settled over the call.
The commissioner seemed almost reluctant to continue.
"I watched the footage three times."
His voice carried a trace of disbelief.
"The bars didn’t break because they were damaged. Damien physically bent them apart."
Stan’s fingers stopped tapping.
That detail was far more significant than the prison fight itself.

Blackridge’s cell bars were designed to withstand enormous amounts of force. Damien had previously been an ordinary human, at least as far as Stan knew. There was no reason he should have been capable of bending reinforced metal with his bare hands.
Yet the footage apparently showed him doing exactly that.
The commissioner continued.
"He squeezed through the opening and escaped his cell."
"Then what?"
"That’s where things got worse."
The commissioner’s voice became heavier.
"Damien began opening other cells."
Stan slowly leaned forward, his attention now completely fixed on the conversation.
"How?
"The same way."
"He bent the bars?"
"Exactly."
Stan’s eyes narrowed further.
"How many?"
"We haven’t determined the exact number yet. The footage from several sections was damaged during the chaos, but he opened enough cells to release a significant number of prisoners."
For several seconds, Stan didn’t respond.

The information running through his mind was becoming increasingly concerning. Damien had entered prison as an ordinary man. He had been beaten by other inmates, apparently survived injuries that should have left him incapacitated, and then demonstrated physical strength powerful enough to overpower several prisoners and bend reinforced metal bars with his bare hands.
More importantly, he hadn’t simply escaped.
He had created an opportunity for other prisoners to escape alongside him.
It might make him look like a good Samaritan, But Stan knew Damien was just utilising the chaos caused by other prisoners to facilitate his own escape...
Stan’s gaze became cold. "How long was he inside the prison after the first cell was opened?"
The commissioner hesitated.
"We’re still reconstructing the timeline. The chaos made it difficult to determine exactly when certain events occurred, especially after multiple sections of the prison went into lockdown."
"Did the guards confront him?"
"They tried."
"And?"
"The first response team was overwhelmed."
Stan’s expression darkened.
"How many officers were involved?"
"Six initially. More arrived afterward."
"And Damien?"
"He managed to get past them."
"By fighting?"

"Partly. But according to the footage, the situation became chaotic once the other prisoners realized what was happening. Some of them joined Damien, while others simply used the opportunity to escape."
The commissioner sighed.

chapters.title: Chapter 504: Threat Unleashed
paragraphs: Stan's gaze hardened.
That was exactly what he had been afraid of.

Damien was no longer a known threat confined within four walls. He was now an unknown variable somewhere outside the prison, potentially surrounded by other escaped criminals and possessing abilities that he hadn't possessed before entering the facility.
Camilla watched Stan carefully.
She could tell from his expression that the situation had become far more serious than either of them had initially expected.
The commissioner spoke again.
"There's something else."
Stan looked toward the phone. "What?"
"The officers who saw him before the escape all said the same thing."
"What did they say?"
"They said Damien looked different."
Stan's eyes narrowed. "Different how?"

"They couldn't explain it properly. They said there was something about his presence that had changed. He seemed... stronger. More confident. Almost like he knew exactly what his body was capable of."
Stan fell silent.
That detail bothered him more than the prison bars.
An awakening was one thing. But instinctively understanding the changes so quickly was another.

If Damien had only recently comprehended the Dao and become a cultivator, then there should have been at least some period of confusion while he learned what he was capable of. Yet according to the commissioner's description, Damien had quickly transitioned from being beaten by other prisoners to dominating them and escaping his cell.
That suggested either his newfound abilities were exceptionally intuitive, or something else had happened during those hours.
Stan's eyes narrowed as he considered the possibility.
"What happened to the prisoners Damien fought?"
"The ones he attacked?"
"Yes."
"The prison medical team treated them. None of them died, as far as we know."
Stan gave a slight nod.
"And Damien?"
"We don't know."
The answer hung heavily between them.
The commissioner continued, "He disappeared during the evacuation. By the time the authorities regained control of the facility, he was already gone.
Stan slowly leaned back against the sofa again.
For the first time since the call began, his expression became completely unreadable.
Damien Bale had escaped.
And judging from everything the commissioner had told him, the man who had escaped Blackridge Correctional Facility was no longer the same Damien Bale who had been imprisoned there.
Whatever had awakened inside him had given him enough strength to tear through the prison's defenses.
And Stan had a feeling that this was only the beginning.

The sheer fact that Damien had managed to escape from Blackridge Correctional Facility was already troubling, but what concerned Stan even more was how easily the prison seemed to have lost control of the situation.
"Why didn't the guards stop him?" Stan asked, his voice calm but carrying a hint of disbelief. "They had guns."

"They tried," the commissioner replied with a heavy sigh. "According to the officers on the scene, the situation deteriorated extremely quickly. Once several cells were opened, the entire prison descended into chaos. The guards were suddenly dealing with multiple escaped inmates at once, while Damien was moving through the facility like he had nothing left to fear."
The commissioner paused before continuing.

"And there's another factor. The guards aren't authorized to simply execute prisoners, even during a violent escape. They were forced to hesitate before using lethal force, and Damien took advantage of that hesitation."
Stan remained silent for a moment before asking, "Did he simply break his way out, or did he attack the guards?"
"Yes," the commissioner answered immediately.
Stan's brow furrowed slightly.
"Yes?"
"He attacked the guards."
"How many?"

"We don't have an exact number yet. Some officers were injured during the confrontation, while others were forced to retreat to more defensible positions when they realized they were no longer dealing with an ordinary prisoner."
Stan's expression grew more serious.

He had already expected Damien to be stronger after awakening, but the commissioner's description suggested that the difference between the man Damien had been before entering prison and the person who had escaped was enormous.

"And then came the part that convinced me this wasn't simply some unusually strong man," the commissioner continued. His voice became noticeably more serious as he recalled the reports. "Damien encountered an armed response team."
Stan's eyes narrowed slightly.
"A firing squad?"

"Essentially," the commissioner replied. "Several armed officers had their weapons trained directly on him. They ordered him to get on the ground and surrender, but Damien simply stood there and looked at them."
"And he still advanced?"
"Yes."
"Why?
The commissioner gave a humorless laugh.

"Confidence. At least, that's how it appeared. He seemed completely convinced that the officers couldn't stop him. There was no hesitation in his movements, and according to the officers, he didn't appear particularly frightened when he saw the weapons pointed at him."
Stan's expression darkened.
That detail immediately caught his attention.

A normal person facing several armed officers would instinctively understand the danger. Even someone possessing extraordinary physical strength should hesitate when staring down a group of people carrying firearms.
Damien, however, seemed to have developed a dangerous level of confidence after awakening.

"The footage shows Damien standing there while the officers repeatedly ordered him to get on the ground," the commissioner continued. "He ignored every command. The officers were eventually forced to open fire."
Stan's eyes narrowed, but he remained silent, allowing the commissioner to continue.
"Damien moved," the commissioner said. "Very quickly. The officers managed to hit him, but he avoided the majority of the shots."
"But he didn't dodge everything."
"No."
"He was shot?"
"Yes."
Stan's expression changed slightly.
"Then how did he survive?"
There was a brief pause on the other end of the call.
"He grabbed another prisoner."
Stan's eyes immediately sharpened.
"What?"
"He pulled one of the escaping inmates in front of himself and used him as a shield."
For a moment, Stan said nothing.
The commissioner's description painted a very different picture of Damien than the initial reports might have suggested.
Damien had been willing to confront armed officers, but the moment bullets actually started flying, he had instinctively protected himself by sacrificing another prisoner.
"So he was afraid of the guns," Stan concluded.

"That's our assessment," the commissioner replied. "Whatever ability Damien gained seems to have made him extremely strong, but bullets can still hurt him. He clearly understood that, which was why he used the other prisoner as a shield."

chapters.title: Chapter 505: Request
paragraphs: "Whatever ability Damien gained seems to have made him extremely strong, but bullets can still hurt him. He clearly understood that, which was why he used the other prisoner as a shield."
Stan slowly nodded. "That makes sense."

"After that, Damien broke through another section of the facility," the commissioner continued. "By then, the prison was already in complete disorder. Guards were trying to regain control, prisoners were running in every direction, alarms were sounding, and several sections of the facility had effectively become impossible to secure."
"And eventually he escaped?"
"Yes," the commissioner said with another sigh. "Eventually."
Stan leaned back slightly as he processed the information.
Damien had not become invulnerable.
That was useful information.
Strength could be countered. Durability could be measured. If conventional weapons were still capable of injuring him, then Damien was not yet beyond the reach of ordinary forces.
The fact that Damien had not yet reached a level where bullets were meaningless gave Stan confidence in his ability to handle him.
After all, bullets and even bombs were nothing to Stan as of right now.
"So his strength isn't enough to make him invulnerable," Stan said.
"That's what we're assuming."
The commissioner paused.
"Good."
There was a brief silence.
"Good?"
Stan's expression remained serious.
"If guns can still hurt him, then he isn't impossible to stop."
"That's what I told my people."
The commissioner hesitated before continuing.
"But there's something else you need to understand."
"What?"
"His physical strength."
Stan waited.
"The officers estimate that Damien is several times stronger than an ordinary man."
"Several times?" Stan asked. "Do they have any accurate multiplier?"
The commissioner sighed.

"Not yet. We don't have enough data to quantify it accurately. Everything is based on eyewitness reports and the security footage we've recovered. But bending reinforced prison bars with your bare hands is obviously not something a normal human being can do."
"No," Stan agreed.
The commissioner continued, "I know this is going to sound absurd."
"At this point, I'm listening."
"We're beginning to suspect that something happened to Damien while he was in prison. Something that gave him these abilities."
Stan's eyes narrowed.
"You're thinking some kind of enhancement?"
"Exactly. We don't know what caused it, but whatever happened to him fundamentally changed his physical capabilities."
Stan remained quiet.
The commissioner sighed before adding, "We've also heard reports of other people doing strange things recently."
Stan's expression remained unchanged.
"Strange things?"

"Nothing confirmed," the commissioner quickly clarified. "At least, not officially. There have been several unusual incidents reported over the past few days. People surviving injuries they shouldn't have survived. Individuals displaying abnormal physical abilities. Cases that don't make much sense when viewed from a normal perspective."
Stan's gaze became distant.
"So Damien isn't necessarily an isolated case.
"We don't know," the commissioner admitted. "That's the problem. There isn't enough reliable information yet to determine whether these incidents are connected."
Stan didn't answer.
He already knew considerably more than the commissioner realized.
The world was beginning to change, and the awakening of the Dao was only the beginning of what was coming.

Ordinary people were beginning to encounter forces they had never imagined possible, and Damien appeared to have stumbled onto his own path through hatred, resentment, and an overwhelming desire for revenge.
The commissioner eventually broke the silence.
"Stan?"
"I'm here."
"What are you thinking?"
Stan remained quiet for a moment before answering in an almost casual tone.
"That this is quite unbelievable."
"Really?" The commissioner immediately agreed. "It's quite unbelievable that all of this happened inside a supposedly secure correctional facility."
"Exactly."

"Even I was surprised when I first heard about it. In fact, I had to personally ask my colleagues to send me the recordings because I didn't want to rely solely on the initial reports. Some of the things described in those reports sounded so exaggerated that I assumed the officers might have been misinterpreting what they saw."
"And after watching the recordings?"
"I couldn't dismiss it anymore," the commissioner replied. "The footage doesn't lie."
"No," Stan said quietly. "It doesn't."
He leaned back and considered the situation more carefully.
The prison escape itself was serious, but it was not the part that concerned him most.
"What about the other prisoners?" Stan asked.
"We've already recaptured several of them."
"And the rest?"
"They're still being searched for."
"How many?"

"We're still confirming the exact number. The prison was in such chaos that we're having difficulty establishing exactly who escaped and who remained inside. Search teams are working through the surrounding area, while other officers are checking roads, abandoned buildings, transportation routes, and locations where fugitives might seek shelter."
"Good."
"We're treating it as a major manhunt," the commissioner added. "Every available unit in the surrounding area is being informed, and we're coordinating the search as carefully as possible."
Stan nodded slowly.
"That makes sense."
A brief silence settled between them before the commissioner spoke again, his tone becoming noticeably more personal.
"There's another reason why I called you, apart from telling you this."
"What is it?"
"Considering Damien's history with you and Sophie..." The commissioner paused briefly, as though carefully choosing his words. "I'd strongly urge you to be careful."
Stan smiled faintly.
"I'll be okay, Commissioner."
He waved away the concern despite knowing the commissioner could not see the gesture.
"I can handle myself."
"I know," the commissioner replied. "But that doesn't mean you should underestimate him."
"I'm not."
"Good."
The commissioner paused before continuing.
"Because based on everything I've seen and everything the officers have reported, Damien isn't behaving like a normal fugitive."
Stan's expression hardened.
"I figured.

"He deliberately confronted armed officers instead of attempting to avoid them. He escaped from a secure facility, overpowered guards, and demonstrated enough physical strength to break through reinforced barriers. More importantly, from what the officers told me, he seemed unusually confident after discovering what he could do."
"That's dangerous."
"Exactly."
The commissioner took another breath.

"Someone who suddenly gains that kind of strength may not fully understand their own limits. Damien might not know what he can and cannot do yet. He could injure or kill someone simply because he doesn't understand how much force he's capable of using."
Stan remained silent.
That was exactly what made the situation dangerous.
Damien had only just awakened.

He had no proper understanding of his newfound strength, no training, and no discipline. Unlike someone who had spent time learning how to control Qi within them, Damien's first experience with extraordinary power had occurred in the middle of a violent prison escape.
His emotions were already unstable, and his hatred toward Stan and Sophie had only grown stronger during his imprisonment.
Power had now been placed in the hands of someone driven by revenge.
That combination was dangerous.
Stan's fingers tapped lightly against the armrest as he considered everything he had just learned.
The escape itself was only one problem.
The greater problem was that Damien had now entered the outside world with nothing holding him back.
No prison walls.
No guards.
No restraints.
And, most importantly, no reason to suppress the hatred he had been nurturing for so long.
If Damien's first instinct after awakening had been to escape, then Stan could only imagine what his next move would be.
The commissioner suddenly spoke again.
"Stan?"
Stan lifted his eyes.
"Yes?"
"Are you still there?"
"I'm here."
The commissioner hesitated.
"What are you thinking?"
Stan remained silent for several seconds.
His mind was already moving through countless possibilities.
Damien could run.
He could hide.
He could seek out other awakened individuals.
He could attempt to gather criminals around himself.
Or, considering his hatred toward Stan and Sophie, he could do something far more direct.
He could come for them.
Stan's eyes became cold.
If Damien truly intended to pursue revenge, then allowing him to move freely would eventually become a problem.
But Stan wasn't going to wait for that moment.
"Commissioner," Stan finally said.
"Yes?"
"I have a request."

A brief silence settled between them before the commissioner spoke again, his tone becoming noticeably more personal.
"There's another reason why I called you, apart from telling you this."
"What is it?"
"Considering Damien's history with you and Sophie..." The commissioner paused briefly, as though carefully choosing his words.
"I'd strongly urge you to be careful."
Stan smiled faintly.
"I'll be okay, Commissioner."
He waved away the concern despite knowing the commissioner could not see the gesture.
"I can handle myself."
"I know," the commissioner replied.
"But that doesn't mean you should underestimate him."
"I'm not."
"Good."
The commissioner paused before continuing.
"Because based on everything I've seen and everything the officers have reported, Damien isn't behaving like a normal fugitive."
Stan's expression hardened.
"I figured.
"He deliberately confronted armed officers instead of attempting to avoid them.
He escaped from a secure facility, overpowered guards, and demonstrated enough physical strength to break through reinforced barriers.
More importantly, from what the officers told me, he seemed unusually confident after discovering what he could do."
"That's dangerous."
"Exactly."
The commissioner took another breath.
"Someone who suddenly gains that kind of strength may not fully understand their own limits.
Damien might not know what he can and cannot do yet.
He could injure or kill someone simply because he doesn't understand how much force he's capable of using."
Stan remained silent.
That was exactly what made the situation dangerous.
Damien had only just awakened.
He had no proper understanding of his newfound strength, no training, and no discipline.
Unlike someone who had spent time learning how to control Qi within them, Damien's first experience with extraordinary power had occurred in the middle of a violent prison escape.
His emotions were already unstable, and his hatred toward Stan and Sophie had only grown stronger during his imprisonment.
Power had now been placed in the hands of someone driven by revenge.
That combination was dangerous.
Stan's fingers tapped lightly against the armrest as he considered everything he had just learned.
The escape itself was only one problem.
The greater problem was that Damien had now entered the outside world with nothing holding him back.
No prison walls.
No guards.
No restraints.
And, most importantly, no reason to suppress the hatred he had been nurturing for so long.
If Damien's first instinct after awakening had been to escape, then Stan could only imagine what his next move would be.
The commissioner suddenly spoke again.
"Stan?"
Stan lifted his eyes.
"Yes?"
"Are you still there?"
"I'm here."
The commissioner hesitated.
"What are you thinking?"
Stan remained silent for several seconds.
His mind was already moving through countless possibilities.
Damien could run.
He could hide.
He could seek out other awakened individuals.
He could attempt to gather criminals around himself.
Or, considering his hatred toward Stan and Sophie, he could do something far more direct.
He could come for them.
Stan's eyes became cold.
If Damien truly intended to pursue revenge, then allowing him to move freely would eventually become a problem.
But Stan wasn't going to wait for that moment.
"Commissioner," Stan finally said.
"Yes?"
"I have a request."

chapters.title: Chapter 506: Manhunt
paragraphs: "I have a request Commissioner."
"What’s that?"
"Can you deploy some officers around the Inksea Peak University campus?"
The commissioner did not hesitate. "Of course."
"Preferably around Sophie’s and Zoe’s residence." Stan’s tone became slightly firmer as he continued. "And keep an eye out for Damien. If he’s anywhere near the campus, I want to know immediately."
There was a brief silence on the other end of the call before the commissioner responded. "I was planning to do that even without you asking."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "Really?"

"Of course." The commissioner sounded almost offended by the question. "It’s our job to recapture these fugitives. We’re not going to allow someone like Damien to remain at large without taking precautions, especially after what happened at Blackridge."
The commissioner paused for a moment before continuing in a more serious tone. "And now that we have information about Damien’s capabilities, we’re treating him as extremely dangerous."
Stan’s expression grew more serious as well. "What are you planning?"
"I’ll issue instructions to the officers assigned to the manhunt. I’ll make sure the teams operating near Inksea Peak University understand that Damien may possess extraordinary physical strength."
Another brief pause followed before the commissioner continued.
"If Damien is located and presents an immediate threat to the officers or civilians around him, they’re authorized to use lethal force, guns and ammunituon."

Stan’s gaze sharpened slightly at those words. He understood why the police had reached that conclusion. From their perspective, Damien was an escaped prisoner who had already demonstrated physical abilities far beyond what an ordinary human should possess. They had no understanding of cultivation or the Dao, so they could only categorize what they had witnessed according to the concepts available to them.
"Make sure they don’t underestimate him," Stan said.
"They won’t."
"And Commissioner?"
"Yes?"
"Don’t forget to inform me if he’s spotted."
"You’ll be one of the first people I contact."
"Good."
The commissioner gave a quiet chuckle. "Still trying to get involved in police business?"
"Only when it concerns my friends."
"I figured."

They exchanged a few more words before eventually ending the call. Once the connection was severed, Stan slowly lowered his phone and stared at the dark screen for several seconds. The conversation had been brief, but the implications were not. Damien was somewhere outside the prison now, and unlike before, he possessed enough strength to make himself a serious threat to ordinary people.
The room gradually returned to silence.

Camilla, who had been listening to the conversation from nearby, turned toward him. Her expression was thoughtful as she considered everything she had just heard. She had remained quiet throughout the call, allowing Stan to handle the matter without interruption, but her curiosity was obvious.
"So..." she began, breaking the silence. "This Damien comprehended Dao?"
"Most likely," Stan replied.
"And the police think it’s some kind of superpower."
"They don’t know any better."

Camilla nodded slowly. From the perspective of ordinary people, Damien’s sudden increase in strength could only be explained through concepts they already understood. They had no knowledge of the Dao, cultivation, awakening, or the deeper changes that were beginning to spread throughout the world. To them, someone suddenly gaining extraordinary physical abilities was simply another unexplained dao comprehension.
Stan, however, knew that there was much more to it than that.

He had seen firsthand what the awakening of the Dao could lead to, and Damien’s situation was particularly concerning because his breakthrough had been triggered by hatred and revenge. Unlike someone who had calmly begun cultivating under proper guidance, Damien had stumbled into power while consumed by emotions that had already distorted his judgment.
"Do you really think he’s dangerous?" Camilla asked.
Stan leaned back against the sofa and considered the question carefully. His expression remained calm, but there was a noticeable seriousness in his eyes.
"Right now?" he asked.
Camilla waited.
Stan took a moment before answering. "Not enough to threaten me."
Camilla continued watching him, waiting for him to elaborate.

"But he’s dangerous to ordinary people," Stan added. "A person with that level of strength, combined with Damien’s current mental state, could cause considerable damage before anyone manages to stop him. And I have my girls to protect."

His voice remained steady, but the meaning behind his words was clear. Stan was not worried about Damien overpowering him. He was concerned about what Damien might do before someone strong enough to restrain him arrived. Even a relatively weak cultivator could become a terrifying threat when placed among ordinary people, especially if that cultivator had no concern for consequences.

Stan’s gaze gradually drifted toward the window. Beyond the glass, the world looked deceptively normal. The streets were still filled with people going about their daily lives, and nothing about the quiet surroundings suggested that humanity was standing at the beginning of a profound transformation.
"More importantly," he continued, his voice becoming quieter, "he’s only just begun."
Camilla followed his gaze toward the window but did not immediately respond.

Damien had awakened through hatred. He had discovered strength through revenge, and for the first time in his life, he now possessed the physical power to act on the emotions that had consumed him for so long. That combination was far more dangerous than strength alone.
Stan understood that the prison escape was not the end of Damien’s story. If anything, it was the beginning.

The hatred that had awakened Damien’s power was not something that would simply disappear now that he had escaped. If anything, possessing newfound strength might encourage those emotions to grow even stronger. With every victory, every confrontation, and every opportunity to pursue his revenge, Damien could become more convinced that his hatred was justified.
And if his strength continued to grow alongside that hatred, even Stan could not predict what Damien might eventually become.
For several moments, neither of them spoke.

Eventually, Stan’s attention shifted toward the chessboard in front of them. Their game had been interrupted by the phone call, leaving the pieces exactly where they had been when the conversation began. Camilla’s previous move remained on the board, while Stan’s pieces waited for his response.
Rather than continuing the discussion about Damien, Stan reached forward and calmly moved one of his pieces.
Camilla blinked when she noticed what he had done.
"You made a move?"
"Of course."
"While thinking about that Damien?"
Stan glanced at her. "Why not?"

Camilla looked down at the chessboard and began studying the position. She initially appeared confident, but that confidence quickly disappeared as she traced the implications of Stan’s move. After a few seconds, her expression changed when she realized what he had done.
"...You trapped me."
A small smile appeared on Stan’s face. "You were distracted."
Camilla narrowed her eyes at him. "That’s cheating."
"It’s not."
"You waited until I was distracted."
"That’s strategy."
She stared at him for several seconds, clearly unconvinced by his defense. Eventually, however, the irritation in her expression gave way to a faint smile.
"Fine."
She moved one of her pieces and leaned back slightly. "Then I’ll use strategy too."
Stan chuckled.

The conversation about Damien gradually faded into the background as the two of them returned their attention to the chessboard. For the moment, there was nothing more Stan could personally do. The police had been alerted, officers were already searching for Damien, and Sophie’s residence would receive additional protection.
Outside, the search for Damien Bale had already begun.

Police teams were spreading throughout the surrounding areas, checking locations where an escaped prisoner might attempt to hide or seek assistance. Additional officers were being positioned near Inksea Peak University, particularly around Sophie’s residence, while others continued following every available lead connected to the prison escape.
Yet Damien remained somewhere beyond their reach.

He was no longer the ordinary man he had been before entering Blackridge Correctional Facility. Somewhere along the path of hatred and revenge, he had taken his first step into a world that ordinary people did not yet understand.
He possessed newfound strength that he barely understood, a newly awakened comprehension of the Dao, and a hatred that had already begun shaping his decisions.
Stan knew better than most that once someone awakened to power, their life would never be ordinary again.
And Damien Bale had only just awakened.

chapters.title: Chapter 507: Changes
paragraphs: With the coming of Qi, the world changed.

However, the world did not change all at once. There was no single explosion that shook the planet, no announcement from the heavens declaring that humanity had entered a new age, and no brilliant flash of light that suddenly transformed ordinary people into extraordinary beings. The change began so quietly that most of humanity remained completely unaware of it.

At first, the changes were so subtle that they could easily be dismissed as coincidences. A few athletes performed slightly better than expected. Some patients recovered from injuries a little faster than doctors anticipated. Certain plants grew unusually quickly, while animals in isolated regions began displaying strange increases in strength and vitality. None of these incidents were extraordinary enough to immediately attract global attention.
Then the changes became more frequent.

What had once been isolated incidents began appearing in different parts of the world, separated by thousands of kilometers and seemingly unrelated to one another. Scientists noticed abnormalities in their measurements. Doctors began encountering patients who recovered faster than expected. Athletes began breaking records that had once seemed almost impossible to surpass.
At first, humanity simply adjusted its expectations.
Then the records began falling too quickly.
And eventually, the changes became impossible to ignore.
GLOBAL NEWS NETWORK — 6:42 A.M.
"Another Record Falls as Track Star Posts Unprecedented Time."

The footage showed a young sprinter crossing the finish line at breathtaking speed. His body leaned forward as he pushed himself through the final meters, every muscle in his legs visibly straining beneath his skin. The moment he crossed the line, the stadium erupted into thunderous cheers.
Yet the athlete himself did not celebrate immediately.

Instead, he stood frozen on the track, staring at the scoreboard with a bewildered expression. His chest rose and fell rapidly as he tried to catch his breath, while the numbers displayed above him seemed almost impossible to comprehend.

His previous personal best had already been enough to place him among the fastest runners in his country. He had spent years training to shave fractions of a second from his time, enduring injuries, exhausting practices, strict diets, and countless hours of conditioning for improvements that were often measured in hundredths of a second.
Now, he had suddenly surpassed that record by a margin that should have required years of additional training.
More importantly, his new time was fast enough to break the national record.
The commentators initially assumed there had been an error.

The timing equipment was checked immediately. Officials examined the sensors, reviewed the footage, and repeated their calculations. Some even questioned whether the starting mechanism had malfunctioned and given the athlete an unfair advantage.
But the equipment was functioning perfectly.
There was no mistake.
The record stood.
The incident attracted international attention, but it was still treated as an extraordinary sporting achievement rather than evidence of something fundamentally wrong with the world.
That assumption lasted only a few hours.
SPORTSNET — 9:15 A.M.
"Three National Records Broken in One Day."
By midmorning, another report had appeared.
Then another.

A professional swimmer had shattered a long-standing national record by a margin that stunned his coaches. A weightlifter had successfully lifted an amount of weight that, only weeks earlier, had been considered far beyond his realistic physical limit. Somewhere else, a marathon runner had completed his race nearly four minutes faster than his previous personal best despite following essentially the same training routine he had used for years.
What made the situation particularly strange was that these athletes were not connected.

They came from different countries, trained under different coaches, followed different diets, and competed in completely different sports. There was no shared supplement, training program, piece of equipment, or medical treatment that could explain their sudden improvements.
Yet they had all achieved extraordinary results within the same twenty-four-hour period.

Sports scientists began appearing on television programs to discuss the phenomenon. Some suggested that improvements in training methods had finally reached a point where their effects were becoming visible. Others attributed the results to better nutrition, advanced recovery techniques, psychological conditioning, or improvements in sports equipment.
A few experts suggested that statistical coincidence could explain the unusual concentration of record-breaking performances.
The explanations sounded reasonable.
At least for a while.
Then another record fell.
And another.
And another.
Within days, the number of abnormal performances had grown too large for coincidence to remain a convincing explanation.
The world began paying attention.
Yet the strangest changes were not occurring inside stadiums.
They were happening inside hospitals.
WORLD HEALTH REPORT — 11:03 A.M.
"Hospitals Report Unexpected Reduction in Recovery Times."

Compared with the sporting records, the medical reports initially received very little attention. There were no cheering crowds, no dramatic photographs, and no famous athletes involved. The changes appeared small enough that most people considered them unimportant.
Doctors in several hospitals, however, had begun noticing something unusual.
Patients recovering from routine procedures appeared to be healing slightly faster than expected.

The difference was not dramatic. Nobody was waking up from surgery completely healed, and no doctor was claiming that impossible medical miracles had occurred. Instead, the changes were subtle but measurable.

Wounds that normally required several days to close properly were showing signs of healing earlier than expected. Patients recovering from minor injuries were regaining mobility faster. Bruising disappeared sooner. Small cuts and abrasions seemed to heal at rates that were consistently above established averages.
At first, doctors assumed the differences were simply statistical fluctuations.

Medicine dealt with probabilities, after all. Human bodies did not always follow averages perfectly. Some patients healed faster than others, while some required more time than expected. A handful of unusual recoveries meant very little by themselves.
Then hospitals in other countries began reporting similar observations.
The differences remained small, but they were remarkably consistent.

Researchers began quietly collecting data. Medical institutions started comparing recovery times across different populations, age groups, climates, and treatment methods. Scientists examined blood samples, cellular activity, metabolic rates, and countless other biological indicators in an attempt to determine whether something had changed.
They did not yet know what they were searching for.
They only knew that something was happening.
And whatever it was, it appeared to be happening everywhere.
